title: Vendor Query Retention Tiering and Cost Allocation Schedule
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working draft of a retention-tier and cost allocation schedule that we can attach to vendor contracts (or append to existing DPAs) for managed inference providers. Focus is on query logs, ephemeral KV/prefix caches, telemetry traces, and sampled inference artifacts (e.g., for quality monitoring). Not intended to replace full DPA — it is a schedule/attachment that makes retention and billing transparent for security, legal, and finance review.

High-level principles (redlines for contract):
- Minimize retention: default to shortest tier that satisfies operational needs.
- Tiering by purpose: separate retention by reason (SRE/debug, billing/usage, quality/eval, compliance/legal hold).
- Cost transparency: clearly call out per-GB/month and per-retrieval fees for each tier, and allocation method when customer data is commingled.
- Sampling & redaction: default to pseudonymize before storing for quality; store raw query only under explicit customer opt-in and clear legal basis.
- Auditability: vendor must retain immutable retention-change logs and provide evidence of deletion on request within X days.

Retention tiers (recommended defaults) — company-facing names and draft clause text:
1) Ephemeral cache ("ephemeral-0"): 0-7 days
   - Purpose: KV/prefix caches and in-memory request buffers used to accelerate low-latency inference.
   - Storage behavior: primarily in-memory; persisted only for crash-recovery with automatic TTL.
   - Redaction: do not persist raw PII; apply token-level mask for any persisted state.
   - Billing: included in serving fee; no separate storage charge.
   - Draft clause snippet: "Vendor shall retain ephemeral cache data for no longer than seven (7) days and shall not use persisted cache for training or model improvement except as expressly permitted in this Agreement."

2) Operational logs ("ops-30"): 30 days
   - Purpose: SRE, incident investigation, capacity planning.
   - Contents: request/response metadata, error traces, anonymized latency traces. Raw prompts should not be stored unless flagged.
   - Access: role-restricted to SRE and on-call.
   - Billing: low per-GB/month storage fee; sample pricing: $0.02 per GB-month.
   - Clause snippet: "Operational logs retained for thirty (30) days. Vendor will provide redacted request IDs and reconstructed traces on request subject to audit scope."

3) Short-term retention for billing ("billing-90"): 90 days
   - Purpose: dispute resolution, usage reconciliation.
   - Contents: usage counters, per-request metadata, minimal prompt hash (not full prompt) unless customer requires raw for dispute.
   - Billing: $0.05 per GB-month; retrieval fee $25 per retrieval (first 5 retrievals per month free).
   - Clause snippet: "Usage records required for billing disputes retained for ninety (90) days. Retrievals for billing disputes are subject to the retrieval fee schedule below."

4) Quality sampling / eval store ("eval-180"): 180 days (default)
   - Purpose: model quality monitoring, A/B evals, regression checks.
   - Contents: sampled request+response pairs, with redaction/pseudonymization applied by default.
   - Sample rate: vendor to document sampling methodology; default rate 0.1% of requests or deterministically by hashed customer ID.
   - Billing: $0.15 per GB-month; retrieval $50.
   - Clause snippet: "Vendor will provide customer with documentation of sampling methodology and will pseudonymize samples by default. Raw samples retained only where customer consents."

5) Long-term legal/compliance archive ("legal-archive"): 1–7 years (by exception)
   - Purpose: legal holds, regulatory audits, export control retention.
   - Activation: only via written request from Customer or legal process; vendor to notify immediate cost impact.
   - Storage: encrypted, access-controlled cold storage.
   - Billing: higher storage and retrieval fees (e.g., $0.40 per GB-month; retrieval $200; expedited retrieval additional).
   - Clause snippet: "Long-term retention only upon Customer instruction or lawful requirement; associated costs billed per schedule."

6) Incident forensics snapshot ("forensics-temp"): up to 2 years but by exception only
   - Purpose: major breach investigations or litigation.
   - Activation: joint written approval, narrow scoping, with deletion certification at end.

Sampling, redaction and privacy controls (operational notes):
- Default: sample -> pseudonymize -> store. Pseudonymization approach: deterministic hashing of user identifiers with per-customer salt; remove contiguous PII segments using rule-based redaction and optional NER.
- Raw retention opt-in: customers can opt into more permissive sampling and raw retention for evals, with explicit checkbox in onboarding and explicit DPA amendment.
- Access controls: sampled data access requires a documented access request; maintain access logs with 90-day retention; privileged accesses trigger alerts to customer security contact.
- Data minimization checklist (for vendor): retention TTL enforcement, automated deletion workflows, cryptographic key rotation, and monthly retention audits stored in confluence link.

Cost allocation and invoicing mechanics (finance-facing):
- Billing lines: serving fee (per-token), storage tier fees (per GB-month per tier), retrieval fees (per retrieval), sampling surcharge (if sample rate > baseline), legal-hold surcharge (per-day).
- Allocation model: when storage pools are shared across multiple customers use either (a) per-customer accounting by tagging at ingestion (preferred), or (b) pro-rata allocation by usage volume over the billing period (fallback). Must disclose method in onboarding packet.
- Example rate table (draft numbers — adjust w/finance):
   * ephemeral-0: $0.00 (included)
   * ops-30: $0.02 / GB-month
   * billing-90: $0.05 / GB-month; $25 retrieval fee
   * eval-180: $0.15 / GB-month; $50 retrieval fee
   * legal-archive: $0.40 / GB-month; $200 retrieval fee; $5/day hold surcharge
- Billing cadence: monthly; retrieval fees charged on next invoice; legal-hold surcharges billed pro-rata monthly.
- Dispute handling: customers may request bill line-item export; vendor must provide raw usage export (CSV) for disputed period within 7 business days.

Auditability and evidence of deletion:
- Deletion certificate: vendor to provide a signed deletion certificate (machine-signed ok) within 10 business days of deletion request that includes retention-ID, deletion timestamp, hashes of deleted blobs, and proof of TTL enforcement.
- Immutable logs: vendor maintains append-only retention-change log (S3 + WORM or equivalent) for minimum of 2 years.
- Penetration testing and attestation cadence: annual pen test and semi-annual attestation for retention enforcement controls.

Contract attachment language (short templates) — pick and adapt:
- "Retention Schedule: The parties agree that the Vendor will apply the retention tiers and billing schedule set forth in the attached Vendor Query Retention Tiering and Cost Allocation Schedule, which is incorporated into the DPA by reference. Any retention beyond the default tiering requires Customer instruction and will be subject to additional fees."
- "Deletion Evidence: Upon Customer request, Vendor will provide deletion evidence including deletion timestamp and cryptographic proof of removal within ten (10) business days."

Operational runbook notes (internal / TODO):
- TODO: confirm retrieval fee amounts with Finance and Competitive Pricing.
- TODO: finalise sampling default (0.1% vs 0.05%); run small pilot.
- Action: Product to add onboarding checkbox and explicit opt-in flow in Console for raw eval retention. (Owner: Priya, due 2024-12-15).
- Question: legal-hold surcharge model — flat fee or per-GB? Recommend hybrid (flat admin fee + per-GB incremental).
- Implementation note: tag data at ingestion with retention-tier label; ensure all worker pools respect TTL enforcement.

Evidence artifacts and links:
- retention enforcement design doc: confluence:security/retention-implementation (link internal)
- sample deletion certificate template: github:legal/templates#deletion-cert
- pricing model draft: spreadsheet (finance) link: confluence:finance/vendor-pricing-retention-draft

Risks / negotiation points (customer-facing):
- Customer pushback expected on sampling pseudonymization; be prepared with clear privacy-preserving technical appendix.
- Legal holds: customers want low-latency retrievals and cheap storage; need to surface cold-storage costs and retrieval delta.
- Commingled storage: customers in regulated industries likely to require per-customer logical separation and tagging; recommend recommending Dedicated storage add-on for those customers.

Sign-off & next steps:
- Internal review by Legal + Finance + Product required.
- Draft to Legal: Aisha (owner) -> review deadline 2024-12-01.
- After internal sign-off, propose as optional schedule in new-customer DPA templates; track adoption and disputes in JIRA INF board.

Draft notes (informal):
- This is a working schedule — we should keep price points intentionally negotiable for enterprise deals.
- Need to avoid wording that implicitly allows training on retained query samples. Always require an explicit training clause.
- Lean toward default pseudonymization, not deletion, for quality workflows — deletion hinders root-cause and regression checks. But legal and regulated customers will override.

End of draft.

Revision log (edits):
- 2024-11-20: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-10: added pricing table + sampling defaults (Liam)
- 2025-01-12: updated auditability language and deletion certificate spec (Priya)
